open_points.subject: flow composition authorization
open_points.text: “Agent — any language-model agent acting for the owner. Reads, authors functions and flows ... the token says whether the agent may author.” conflicts with “compose and prove a flow | agent” and M13’s “from an agent's composition,” which do not require the author right.
open_points.question: Must an agent have the may-author right to create a Flow or FlowVersion, and does the rule differ between creating a new flow and adding a version to an existing flow?
options: May-author is required for every composition
Any authenticated agent may compose flows
May-author is required only to create a new Flow, not to add versions
open_points.default_guess: Require may-author for every flow composition because composing creates authored durable models.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: M08 says “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict,” but also includes `trial_executions` and `decided_at` as facts and says every admission runs every active case again; M09 expressly allows admission after a submission that is “new or reused.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is admitted again over the unchanged corpus, is the result the existing AdmissionVerdict, a new verdict entity, or a new value distinguished by its new execution evidence?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and its original evidence
Create a new AdmissionVerdict entity for each admission
Create a distinct value identified by the new TrialExecutions and decision time
Keep one semantic verdict value and model each admission run separately
open_points.default_guess: Keep the deterministic verdict as a value and introduce a separate admission-run entity for each fresh batch of TrialExecutions.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: M23 declares “Identity: value” but its evidence says “an attempt's record is issued once,” and other models identify it by `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index` and `attempt_number`; M07 classifies an issued execution observation as an entity.
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution an entity representing one particular attempt, identified by its attempt coordinates, or a substitutable value identified by all of its facts?
options: Entity with the attempt-coordinate tuple as its identity
Value containing the attempt coordinates as meaning facts
Separate an attempt entity from an immutable trace-value snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Treat NodeExecution as an entity identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`.

open_points.subject: capture a failed execution
open_points.text: Capture refuses an execution “whose run was already released (its files are gone),” but K-10 also removes the spool whenever a run ends `succeeded`, `refused` or `cancelled`; those runs are never released and can still contain an earlier failed function execution.
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, especially when its inputs included spooled files whose bytes have already been removed?
options: Refuse capture whenever any required input bytes are unavailable
Permit capture after any unreleased run and define another source for the removed file bytes
Permit value-only captures after such runs but refuse captures needing removed files
Allow capture only while the run is active or while a failed run remains unreleased
open_points.default_guess: Permit capture when all required inputs remain available; refuse it when a required spooled file has already been removed.
